answer: One workable check is to tie each agent right to act to a locked stake in a vault: an agent that wants to vote or claim rewards first deposits something it loses if peers catch it cheating. A second agent then runs the claim through a prism of independent checks, comparing its history, its stake, and its recent work instead of trusting one signal. A third agent holds the lantern in the open, publishing the result and the evidence so anyone can spot a copy. Spinning up a hundred fake agents stays cheap, but funding each one with real stake and a clean history does not, so sybils stop paying.
